newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai Securities Building raises costs.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai Securities Building raises costs.

text.p: The most expensive building in Shanghai's premier economic development zone has raised its selling price to $3,000 per sq metres (10.7 sq ft), from $2,700, Shanghai Securities News said on Sunday.
The new rate for floorspace in the Shanghai Securities Building, in Pudong New Area across the Huangpu River from Shanghai's city centre, was introduced on March 1, it said.
Built in the image of the Arc de Triomphe in Paris, the 27-storey building cost $150 million and is the only one in Pudong built of steel and glass, instead of concrete, it said.
Its two office towers cover 118,000 sq metres (1.27 million sq ft). It also has a bridge spanning 63 metres (207 ft), it said.
The Shanghai Securities Exchange will move to the building in May and will occupy the first nine floors, the newspaper said. The other floors are for sale or lease.

Since October 1996, more than 6,000 sq metres (64,200 sq ft) of floor space in the building has been bought by Chinese and overseas securities companies and financial institutions paying $2,700 a sq metres (10.7 sq ft) it said.
